strategy.reason: Block swaps can restructure multi-day work/off sequences to satisfy min/max consecutive working days and consecutive days off simultaneously, and can also incidentally reduce weekend-related penalties while keeping daily coverage stable.
strategy.avoid: Avoid coverage_fill because optimal_coverage_cost is not dominant and adding shifts risks increasing total_assignment_cost and weekend overages; also avoid simple single-day reassign that may not resolve multi-day consecutive patterns.

strategy.reason: Single-day swaps are less likely than block swaps to create illegal_succession chains, while still allowing us to break long work streaks / fix too-short off blocks and potentially reduce weekend and preference penalties without changing total coverage.
strategy.avoid: Avoid block_swap for now due to repeated illegal_succession hard violations; also avoid coverage_fill because several nurses are already at/over max_total and adding shifts risks increasing total_assignment_cost and weekend overages.

strategy.reason: Weekend penalties are large and concentrated; block_reassign can move weekend assignments off over-limit nurses onto nurses with weekend capacity while potentially also repairing consecutive work/off patterns. Compared to block_swap, it can be guided to move coherent weekend blocks and reduce over-max totals for heavily loaded nurses (e.g., Stefaan/Nguyen) without needing complex cross-nurse shift-type exchanges.
strategy.avoid: Avoid block_swap patterns that previously triggered illegal_succession; also avoid coverage_fill since adding shifts risks increasing total_assignment_cost and worsening weekend overages for already heavily scheduled nurses.

strategy.reason: Single-day swaps preserve coverage and are less likely than block moves to introduce illegal_succession, while directly addressing the largest penalties (consecutive work/off patterns) and can also shift weekend work away from over-limit nurses.
strategy.avoid: Avoid block_swap due to repeated illegal_succession hard violations; avoid coverage_fill because several nurses are at/over max_total and adding shifts can worsen total_assignment_cost and weekend overages.

strategy.reason: Block reassign can move coherent multi-day work blocks off the most problematic nurses (e.g., those with weekend overages and streak violations) to nurses with capacity, directly addressing consecutive work/off patterns and weekend counts while avoiding the shift-sequence entanglement that made block_swap prone to illegal_succession.
